attributes.nuance_translation: A word that is used to show that (A) is quite (B), or sometimes used simply to say no thanks.

attributes.body:
結構（けっこう） is a な-Adjective that is actually used more frequently as a sentence altering adverb, than it is as a な-Adjective. What this means is that it is regularly used before an entire phrase (without な or だ), and it will modify the entire sentence. The most common meaning that 結構（けっこう） has is 'quite' (a bit/a lot).

Fun Fact

結構（けっこう） is used very similarly in Japanese to 'no thank you', or 'I'm fine thanks' in English. For example, if someone asks you if you want to try a sample in a shop, most people would just say 結構（けっこう）です.

attributes.description: Differences from ずいぶん、けっこう

attributes.body: Both なかなか and けっこう are adverbs used to express extent. In affirmative sentences, they can both mean 'quite' or 'rather.' A key difference is that なかなか is often used in negative sentences to express difficulty in doing something. Meanwhile, けっこう can be used alone (especially as けっこうです) to politely decline something, like saying 'I'm fine.'
